land.text: Sindh, the Habbari emirate of Mansura

predecessors.note: The Habbari page ends the dynasty with the Ghaznavid conquest of Mansura in 1026; the Soomra page lists Khafif (1010-1026) first.

successors.note: 'Successor: Samma Dynasty' (undated on the page); Cliopatria's Samma row begins in 1344, seven years before the Soomra end.

capitals.name: Mansura (Brahmanabad)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Mansura (1026)'. Thari (Badin District) is listed 'without a date'; the Mansura page says the city 'never recovered' and was later 'ruled by the Soomro Emirs'. The later seat is page silent.

rulers.name: Soomar
rulers.note: Rulers' table of the Soomra page; the page calls the early history 'unclear'. Its lifespan for Chanesar (to 1371) contradicts his 1237 reign end and is a typo on the page.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1026-1027, the end of Cliopatria's 1018 shape: the Soomras 'probably centered in lower Sindh' took over from the Habbari capital Mansura (infobox 'Mansura (1026)'). The Sindh province is used as for the Habbari shapes.

Cliopatria keeps the Habbari label; the Soomras hold Sindh (tributary of the Ghaznavids only 1026-1030). Same correction as the Habbari shapes: Uch and the Multan side belonged to the Multan emirate (Ghor page, 1175).

Same correction. The Soomra page says the Ghaznavids and Ghurids 'continued to rule parts of Sindh, across the eleventh and early twelfth century', undated and unplaced; the Soomras are listed as rulers throughout (Bhoongar I 1053-1068, Dodo I 1068-1092, Sanghar to 1107).
Same correction (Khafif II 1107-1142, Umar I 1142-1181). Unverified beyond the ruler table: page budget.

correction.text: Sindh, the Soomra realm, a Ghurid tributary from 1182

keyframe_review.note: Same correction. Debal and the Soomras are subjugated by Muhammad of Ghor in 1182 (tributaries, not annexed: Sindh passes after 1206 to Bhungar II); Cliopatria's Ghurid row, which reaches 24.8N from 1177, overlaps this shape.
Same correction; the Ghurid conquests of 1186-1194 (Lahore, Delhi) are in the north.
Same correction; Cliopatria ends the row in 1201 although the Soomras last to 1351.

New keyframe for 1202-1351, where Cliopatria has no Sindh shape before the Sind-Samma row of 1344. The Ghor page's infobox gives Sindh to Bhungar II bin Chanesar (Soomra, 1195-1226) after 1206 and Multan to Qabacha; the Soomra page lists rulers to 1351. Extent unverified: page budget; the page says only 'probably centered in lower Sindh'. fx-35 (1 Nov 2026): valid 1202-1319 only; from 1320 the keyframes soomra-dynasty_1320 and _1344 take upper Sind out of the realm.

correction.text: Sindh without the part of upper Sind inside Delhi's Cliopatria outline, 1320-1343: lower Sindh round Thatta and north-western Sind, where the Soomras were 'probably centered in lower Sindh'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1320-1343 (fx-35, from a fx-12 handoff): the realm without the part of upper Sind that the tughlaq-dynasty keyframes of 1320-1343 draw as Delhi's. The Soomra page says 'the Soomras were probably centered in lower Sindh' and 'The precise delineations have yet to be discovered'; the Samma page has 'in 1333 the Sammas were in rebellion', 'The Sammas overthrew the Soomras soon after 1335' and the Samma capital at Samanagar (modern Thatta); the Iltutmish page has Delhi annexing 'large parts of Punjab and Sindh' in 1228 and the Soomra king 'submitted to Iltutmish' and continuing as a vassal (undated); the Muhammad bin Tughluq page has only the 1351 campaign in Sindh 'against Taghi'. No page opened says who governed upper Sindh in 1320-1351, so this is a reading: Delhi's share of Sind is Cliopatria's Khalji outline of 1314 inside the province, minus lower Sindh round Thatta (220 km, the same reading as in the tughlaq-dynasty keyframes, not a page figure). The whole-province outline overlapped tughlaq-dynasty by 158 cells in 1320-1343, which the size rule gave to the Soomras. A plain lower-Sindh disk (the handoff's first proposal) would have left the 98 cells of north-western Sind outside Cliopatria's Delhi outline (Larkana, Dadu, Jacobabad, 67.2-70.1 E, 26.3-28.5 N) to nobody, so they stay Soomra. 1026-1319 is unchanged (whole province): the Mamluk and Khalji overlap with it is settled by the size rule and is not changed here. The Samma page dates the Soomra end both 'soon after 1335' and 1351 (infobox); the dossier keeps 1351.

minus.text: lower Sindh round Thatta (a reading: the lower Indus plain from Karachi and Hyderabad to Umerkot; no page gives bounds), the same disk as the tughlaq-dynasty keyframes leave out
upper Sind inside Cliopatria's Tughlaq and Sind-Samma outlines of 1344, without lower Sindh: the part the tughlaq-dynasty keyframes of 1344-1350 draw

correction.text: Sindh without the part of upper Sind inside Delhi's Cliopatria outline, 1344-1351: lower Sindh round Thatta and north-western Sind

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1344-1351 (fx-35): the same reading with the upper Sind that the tughlaq-dynasty keyframes of 1344-1350 draw (Cliopatria's Tughlaq and Sind-Samma outlines of 1344 inside the province, minus lower Sindh round Thatta): 175 cells instead of 158. Sammas 'overthrew the Soomras soon after 1335' (Samma page); the Soomra infobox keeps the dynasty to 1351 ('Soomra dynasty ends: 1351 (Continued in exile until 1440 in Umerkot)'), as does this dossier. Delhi's expedition against Sindh came in 1351 (Samma page: 'Mohammad bin Tughlaq made an expedition against Sindh in 1351 and died at Sondha').

ledger.note: 1026: the Soomras rise in Sindh. 'Soomra dynasty begins: 1026' (infobox; capital 'Mansura (1026)'), Soomar's reign listed 1026-1053; 'Tributary of the Ghaznavids (1026-1030)'. The page: 'The early history of Soomras is unclear' and they were 'probably centered in lower Sindh'.
1351: the Soomra dynasty ends. 'Soomra dynasty ends: 1351 (Continued in exile until 1440 in Umerkot)'; successor 'Samma Dynasty' (undated on the page). Cliopatria's Sind-Samma row starts in 1344.

wars.name: Ghurid campaign in Sindh
wars.outcome: Multan and Uch taken from the Qarmatian ruler Khafif in 1175; Debal taken and the Soomras subjugated in 1182. No Soomra land is recorded as annexed.
wars.note: The Ghaznavid page is silent on 1175 and 1182.

certainty.note: The Soomra page gives no extent ('probably centered in lower Sindh'); the Indus delta coast is the only firm edge.

notes:
SOOMRA DYNASTY (split from Cliopatria's 'Sind-Habbari Dynasty', sa-03-e). Written from the pages opened for the Habbari dossier (4 of the 5 are cited here); no further pages were opened, so the 1027-1201 shapes are corrected to the province of Sindh on the strength of the Habbari and Muhammad of Ghor pages and the Soomra ruler table only. Extent after 1201 and the end of the dynasty (1351 against Cliopatria's Samma row from 1344) need a gap-filler; suggested pages: Soomra dynasty (full), Samma dynasty, Delhi Sultanate, Multan.

Not recorded as ledger events because the types fit the other side (the Ghurid subjugation of the Soomras at Debal in 1182 is in the war entry; no land changed hands): the Ghaznavid tribute of 1026-1030 (Soomra infobox 'Tributary of the Ghaznavids (1026-1030)') and the Ghurid overlordship from 1182 are vassal_start events for the ghaznavid-empire and ghurid-dynasty dossiers (me-08 / sa-04). Cliopatria draws no Soomra or Sindh shape between 1202 and 1343.
Gazetteer names needed: none beyond the Habbari dossier; the Wikidata id of the Soomra dynasty is not known (null).
